newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends lower on China, mad cow rumor.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends lower on China, mad cow rumor.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures closed lower on Wednesday amid rumors China had purchased South American supplies and talk an Indiana rose grower may have died of Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, traders said.
The Indiana Health Department said it could not confirm press reports that the death of the 62-year-old Indiana man was from CJD but said the state has several cases of CJD annually.
The disease has been called the human version of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), the "madcow" cattle disease that caused a consumer panic in Europe in 1996.
Floor sources largely discounted the rumors but said a scare in the beef industry could limit consumer beef purchases and lessen demand for livestock feed.

Soymeal as further hit by reports China may have bought several cargoes of South American soymeal. Hong Kong trade sources said it was likely China bought a large quantity of soymeal when prices fell. But Argentine traders said they were unsure of the sale.
Soymeal ended $5.70 to $1.70 per ton lower with May off $1.70 at $273.30. Soyoil ended 0.25 to 0.13 lower with May down 0.14 at 24.04.
But losses were limited in old crop contracts by a national port strike in Brazil that could interrupt soybean and soymeal exports, traders said.

A union official on Wednesday said Brazilian stevedores will go on national strike in sympathy with their colleagues at Santos port at 0500 CDT/1000 GMT Friday for 48 hours. Union sources said earlier the strike would begin at 2200 CDT on Thursday.
On the day, Merrill Lynch sold 400 lots May soymeal and 150 lots July, Cargill Inc sold 200 May and 100 each July, August and December but bought 200 lots May and 100 December, pit sources said.
In soyoil, Cargill Inc bought 300 lots May and 400 July while Iowa Grain bought 500 July. Smith Barney sold 300 July and Merrill Lynch sold 200 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 26,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 24,785 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 17,000 lots, against Tuesday's 19,196.
